snippet.title: They Shared a Burrow for 250 Million Years
snippet.description:
A sleeping predator and an injured amphibian ended up in the same burrow. Their unlikely shelter became a fossil that survived for 250 million years.

This paper-diorama short tells the story of Thrinaxodon and Broomistega, two very different animals found together in an ancient South African burrow.

requested.title: Two Ancient Animals Found Together in a 250-Million-Year-Old Burrow
requested.description:
Inside a fossilized burrow about 250 million years old, two very different animals were found together: Thrinaxodon, a small predator, and Broomistega, a young amphibian with injured ribs.

This short follows a possible explanation for how they came to share the shelter and were buried together. The fossil preserves their remains; the animals' final moments are a reconstruction.
